newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel omits key "three is three" remark in speech.
newsitem.headline: Waigel omits key "three is three" remark in speech.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Thursday omitted two key phrases from his speech on monetary union, both of which have caused controversy within the parties in Germany's ruling coalition government.

Waigel dropped the phrases "three is three" and "convergence will determine the timetable", which had been in the printed text of his speech, when addressing a German savings bank conference on monetary union.

Waigel has insisted repeatedly that the economic entry criterion for European monetary union, which calls for a country's budget deficit to be no more than three percent, must be interpreted absolutely strictly.

But the affable Bavarian has come under pressure in the coalition both to ease off and to tighten up on the Maastricht budget deficit target, in the face of growing worries that Germany may not be able to cut its deficits far enough.
He had already backed off calling for a precise "3.0 percent", preferring to speak only of "three percent".
Similarly, his insistence that the level of convergence must take precedence over the timetable for the 1999 start of EMU had been attacked by those who shun a delay in the launch.
Asked after his address why he had omitted the remarks, Waigel gave no clear answer.
"Both the written and the spoken word are valid," he told reporters.
